title: Enterprise onboarding + escalation + integration + QBR playbook (Comprehensive v2)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended process for enterprise customer onboarding, integration guidance, escalation routing, known issues and workarounds, and the cadence and content for health checks / Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and relevant Product/Engineering owners.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-value for new enterprise customers.
- Ensure consistent, predictable escalations and SLAs.
- Provide integration checklists and troubleshooting steps to reduce friction.
- Standardize health checks and QBR metrics and templates.

Scope
- Applies to all new Dedicated and Private deployment customers, and high-touch Hosted customers with enterprise contracts.
- Excludes self-serve SMB onboarding (see quickstarts in eng-developer-experience).

Roles and ownership
- Customer Success (CS): primary onboarding coordinator, QBR owner, health check facilitator.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): integration design, initial testing, data/PKI guidance.
- Support (L1/L2): first-line operational troubleshooting, ticket triage.
- Eng-Platform / Eng-Infra: escalation targets for platform/runtime incidents.
- Security & Compliance: PII/data residency validation, KMS/HSM integration sign-off.

Contact matrix (primary):
- CS Manager: cs-managers@redwood.ai
- SE lead: solutions@redwood.ai
- L2 Support: l2-support@redwood.ai
- On-call runtime engineering (pager): infra-oncall@pager.redwood.ai (follow on-call rota)

Onboarding checklist (90-day template)
1. Kickoff (Week 0)
   - Owner: CS + SE
   - Deliverables: Project plan, success metrics, NDA/KBA checklist, stakeholder map.
   - Actions: Schedule weekly sync, set up shared workspace (Confluence + Slack channel), collect network & IAM requirements.
2. Environment provisioning (Week 1-2)
   - Owner: SE + Customer infra
   - Deliverables: VPC peering (if Private), firewall rules, service account credentials, KMS/HSM integration plan.
   - Example network config table:
     | Item | Recommended value | Notes |
     |------|-------------------|-------|
     | Egress | Allow 52.23.0.0/16 | Redwood control plane endpoints |
     | Ports | 443 outbound; 22 for SFTP only when needed | Use NAT gateway for restricted subnets |
3. Test integration (Week 2-4)
   - Owner: SE + Customer eng
   - Deliverables: End-to-end inference test, authentication validation, sample load test (10-20 RPS).
   - Commands: 
     curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n       -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \n       -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n       -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0", "input":"Hello world"}'

4. Performance validation & SLOs (Week 3-6)
   - Owner: SE + Eng-Platform
   - Deliverables: Latency and throughput baseline, recommendations for batching/quantization, expected cost per 1M tokens.
   - Example acceptance criteria: 95th percentile generation latency < 350ms for 512-token context under warmed cache.
5. Security & compliance validation (Week 4-8)
   - Owner: Security & CS
   - Deliverables: SOC/ISO evidence review, KMS key rotation policy, data residency confirmation.
6. Production rollout (Week 6-12)
   - Owner: CS + SE + On-call
   - Deliverables: Canary rollout plan, rollback conditions, monitoring dashboard links.

Integration guide (reference)
- Common integration patterns:
  - REST API (recommended for most customers): use API keys scoped per-environment.
  - VPC private endpoints: recommended for Private deployments.
  - SDK integration: use official SDKs for retries and streaming.
- Authentication:
  - Use short-lived service tokens where possible; rotate API keys every 90 days.
  - Example header: Authorization: Bearer <SERVICE_TOKEN>
- Best practices:
  - Prefix caching: use consistent prompt prefixes to benefit KV cache.
  - Batching: aggregate small requests when latency-tolerant to improve cost.

Escalation playbook
- Severity definitions:
  - Sev1 (Critical outage): platform unavailable for customer or >50% error rate across routes for >= 5 minutes.
  - Sev2 (Major degradation): significant latency increase or errors impacting core flows (>20% error rate OR latency increases x3 baseline).
  - Sev3 (Partial impact): feature regression, isolated errors, or non-urgent data issues.
  - Sev4 (Informational): general questions, feature requests, non-blocking issues.

Escalation routing steps (when a ticket is opened)
1. Triage (L1 Support, within 15 minutes business hours)
   - Validate scope: collect client id, route/model, timestamp(s), request/response examples, logs (attach sanitized).
   - If reproducible, perform basic checks: API key validity, rate limits, model version, recent deploys.
2. Escalate to L2 (within 60 minutes for Sev1/Sev2)
   - L2 supplies diagnostics: JVM/GPU memory, recent kernel changes, queue sizes, request traces.
3. Pager escalation to Eng-Platform (Sev1)
   - On-call notified via pager duty channel; immediate war room initiated (Slack #incident-<id> + Zoom).
4. Customer comms
   - CS sends status update every 30 minutes for Sev1 until remission, every 2 hours for Sev2, daily for Sev3.

Escalation checklist (must attach to ticket)
- Customer ID and contact list (with escalation names & phone numbers).
- Repro steps and minimal repro script.
- Diagnostic artifacts: logs, traces, sample payloads, error IDs.
- Timeline of events and any recent changes/deploys.

Known issues and workarounds (living table)
- Issue: Intermittent 5xx on model route after kernel rollout
  - Symptoms: Error spikes, stacktrace includes "cudaLaunchFailure"
  - Workaround: Roll back to previous kernel (follow runtime rollback runbook) and restart affected workers.
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime (runtime-team@redwood.ai)
- Issue: Higher-than-expected latency for long prompt sequences
  - Symptoms: T90 latency spikes correlated with >1k token requests
  - Workaround: Use a streaming response pattern + progressive decoding; recommend quantization profile Q4_0 for throughput workloads.
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime / product
- Issue: Customer unable to reach control plane from restricted VPC
  - Symptoms: Failed handshake with control-plane endpoints; TLS errors \
  - Workaround: Ensure outbound rules allow Redwood control-plane IP ranges, confirm TLS interception disabled, or provide private endpoint.
  - Owner: eng-private-deployments

For each known issue maintain the following fields in ticket: first_reported, last_occurrence, workaround, timeline_of_fix, PR_link_to_fix.

Health checks and QBR materials
- Cadence:
  - Weekly health check (first 6 weeks post-production) — 30-minute sync between CS, SE, and customer SRE.
  - Monthly health review (months 2-6) — 30-60 minutes focusing on metrics and operational improvements.
  - Quarterly Business Review (QBR) — strategic session with execs (60 minutes).

- Metrics to collect & present:
  - Availability: uptime % (30d, 90d).
  - Error budget consumption: SLA vs actual (tokens impacted, requests failed).
  - Latency distribution: p50/p90/p99 for generation and embeddings.
  - Cost metrics: $ / 1M tokens, cost variance vs baseline.
  - Usage: active API keys, monthly tokens, peak RPS.
  - Quality signals: regression tests run, prompt eval scores, customer-reported accuracy issues.

QBR agenda (template)
1. Introductions and agenda (5 min)
2. Business outcomes and success metrics recap (10 min)
3. Health and reliability review (15 min)
   - Uptime, SLOs, incidents since last QBR, action status.
4. Cost & performance trends (10 min)
   - Recommendations for batching/quantization or model variant changes.
5. Product roadmap and planned changes (10 min)
6. Action items and next steps (10 min)

Sample QBR slides list (share prior to meeting)
- Executive summary (1 slide)
- Key metrics dashboard screenshot (1-2 slides)
- Major incidents & remediation (1 slide)
- Recommendations & roadmap asks (1-2 slides)

Operational artifacts and templates
- Onboarding project plan template: confluence/customer-success-and-support/templates/onboarding-project-plan
- Escalation notification template (email + Slack):
  Subject: [Sev{1|2}] Incident {INC-####} — {customer-name}
  Body: Include impact, scope, immediate mitigation, next update ETA.
- Minimal repro template (attach to every Sev ticket):
  - Steps to reproduce
  - Expected behavior
  - Observed behavior
  - Sample payloads / logs

Troubleshooting examples
- Check token usage: admin-cli tokens list --customer-id <CID>
- Run a basic generation test to validate model route:
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"test"}' | jq

Appendix: Runbooks and links
- Runtime rollback runbook: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/rollback-runtime-kernel
- Canary rollout checklist: confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/canary-rollout
- SRE incident postmortem template: confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template

Revision history
- 2026-03-01: Created by Aisha Patel (initial consolidated playbook).
- 2026-03-04: Added escalation routing, updated QBR template and known-issues table (reviewers: Marco Diaz, Priya Shah).

Notes and next steps
- CS to adopt this playbook for all enterprise onboardings starting April 2026.
- SE to add automation scripts for the integration testing checklist and surface in the shared onboarding workspace.
